run.procedureSummary: Each of the 5 cycles runs these steps in order, and each step finishes on all six crucibles before the next one starts. (1) Charge: add the cycle's charge list to the six melts, even if that takes a crucible past its volume. (2) Overflow: go through crucibles 1 to 6 in order. If a crucible holds more than its volume, the excess goes into the next crucible before that one is checked, so the excess can cascade. Excess from crucible 6 goes to slag. (3) State check on the melt after overflow: a BASE crucible with melt at or above its upper mark becomes SUPERHEATED. A SUPERHEATED crucible with melt at or below its lower mark becomes BASE. Otherwise the state stays. (4) Return: every transfer is worked out from the melts after the state check, then all are applied at once. A BASE crucible loses floor(melt/4) to slag. A SUPERHEATED crucible sends floor(melt/2) to the crucible before it (i-1); crucible 1's amount goes to slag. Melt a crucible receives here may take it over its volume, and it stays there until the next cycle's overflow. (5) Emergency tap: if the six melts after return total more than 38, each crucible keeps floor(melt/2) and the rest goes to slag. The tap does not change states. I used a Python script for the arithmetic: C:\Users\Jaket\AppData\Local\Temp\om\desk-250\sim.py. I also checked cycle 1 by hand and it matched.

openPoints.point: Which melt the state check uses
openPoints.assumption: The melt after the charge and the full overflow pass, as the step order implies.
The state just set by the same cycle's state check.
All amounts are worked out from the melts before any transfer, then applied at once. A crucible therefore loses or sends an amount based on its own melt before it receives anything.

openPoints.point: Return melt that pushes a crucible over its volume
openPoints.assumption: It stays in that crucible, with no overflow until the next cycle's overflow step, as the write-up says.
'Over 38' means strictly greater than 38. In cycle 5 the total after return is exactly 38, so the tap did not fire.

openPoints.point: When the tap test is made
openPoints.assumption: Once per cycle, on the total after the return step.
Both are inclusive: 'at or above' the upper mark and 'at or below' the lower mark.
Every quarter and half is rounded down (floor). The remainder from a tap goes to slag.
It does not. States change only at the state-check step.
Overflow from crucible 6, the BASE quarter, crucible 1's SUPERHEATED return and the tap remainder all go to slag. Slag is the loss tally.

run.balanceCheck: Starting melt 20 + charges 94 = 114. End melt 38 (6+10+9+7+4+2) + slag 76 = 114. The two sides match.
run.notes: The one figure that turns on an assumption is cycle 5's total after return, which is exactly 38. I read 'over 38' as strictly greater, so the tap did not fire. If 38 itself counted, cycle 5 would also tap: end melt would be [3,5,4,3,2,1], slag 96, and the balance would still hold.
